newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate falls on foreign bank lending.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate falls on foreign bank lending.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 7.7/8.0 percent on Thursday due to lending by foreign banks flush with funds, dealers said.
The overnight traded between 8.5 and 8.9 percent on Wednesday.
"Foreign banks are long and they are offering lower," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "There are also not many borrowers in the market today."
Dealers said interbank rates could dip slightly on Friday following the drop in the overnight.
"Liquidity has not actually improved but rates have been artificially pushed up and should come off slightly," said another Malaysian bank dealer.
Earlier, one-week money was traded at 9.0 percent against 8.8 on Wednesday.
The one-month rate was at 8.5 percent from 8.3, while three-month money was at 8.1 percent against 8.0/8.1.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed, with near-term contracts down while the distant months stayed firmer.
At 0830 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down three points to 92.16, or an implied yield of 7.84 percent.
September contract fell one to 92.39, or 7.61 percent while March 1998 was up one to 92.56, or 7.44 percent.
